code.text:
# rnd-kb-tooling/src/kb_tools/schema.py — the one definition of a brain page
from datetime import date, timedelta
from typing import Annotated, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

Source = Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r"^(RH-\d+|https://\S+)$")]  # a Jira key, or a link to a PR, commit, Drive doc, public thread
RepoGlob = Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r"^(fcp|infrastructure|gitops|byte):\S+$")]  # pages live outside fcp, so name the repo
DAYS = {"30d": 30, "90d": 90, "180d": 180, "365d": 365}


class Page(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    title: str = Field(min_length=8, max_length=100)
    owner: str = Field(pattern=r"^@[\w.-]+(/[\w.-]+)?$")  # a person or @RhinoHealth/<team>; lint checks it is in OWNERS.yml
    reviewed: date
    review_every: Literal["30d", "90d", "180d", "365d"] = "90d"
    confidence: Literal["high", "med", "low"]  # low = AI-drafted, not yet checked by the owner
    sources: list[Source] = Field(min_length=1)
    applies_to: list[RepoGlob] = []
    status: Literal["proposed", "accepted", "superseded"] | None = None  # decisions/ only

    def due(self) -> date:
        return self.reviewed + timedelta(days=DAYS[self.review_every])

    def effective_confidence(self, today: date) -> str:
        # more than 2x overdue reads as low everywhere (search, index, bot); the file itself is not edited
        too_old = (today - self.reviewed).days > 2 * DAYS[self.review_every]
        return "low" if too_old else self.confidence

code.text:
# rnd-kb-tooling/.github/workflows/kb-lint.yml — reusable; rnd-kb calls it on every PR, pinned by SHA
name: kb-lint
on:
  workflow_call:
    secrets:
      KB_APP_ID: { required: true }
      KB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY: { required: true }
      KB_DENY_TERMS: { required: true } # customer names and terms, owned by Security; never stored in a repo
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest # confirm with DevOps: GitHub-hosted or an ARC runner set for these repos
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5 # rnd-kb itself; pin actions by SHA like the infrastructure repo
      - name: gitleaks (before any other repo is checked out)
        run: |
          curl -sSfL https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v8.28.0/gitleaks_8.28.0_linux_x64.tar.gz | tar xz gitleaks
          ./gitleaks dir . --redact --no-banner --exit-code 1
      - id: app
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v2
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.KB_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.KB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: RhinoHealth
          repositories: rnd-kb-tooling,fcp
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with: { repository: RhinoHealth/rnd-kb-tooling, path: .tooling, token: "${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}" }
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with: { repository: RhinoHealth/fcp, path: .repos/fcp, token: "${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}" }
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
      - run: uv run --project .tooling kb lint . --repo fcp=.repos/fcp --index-check
      - run: uv run --project .tooling kb scan . # PHI patterns + deny-list; prints path:line, never the value
        env:
          KB_DENY_TERMS: ${{ secrets.KB_DENY_TERMS }}

code.text:
# fcp

Rhino Health's Federated Computing Platform in one repo: the cloud API, the on-prem client that runs inside
customer networks, the Python SDK and the dashboard.

## Where things live
- `cloud/rhinoCloud/`: cloud API (Django, DRF, Celery). Main app `rhinoCore/`.
- `client/rhinoOnPrem/`: on-prem client (Django, gRPC, RQ). It reaches the cloud over a reverse gRPC stream.
- `common/fcp_common/`: shared code, including the gRPC protos in `rhinoAgentRpc/` (`make protoc`; _pb2 files are committed).
- `sdk/`: the public `rhino_health` package. Read `sdk/CLAUDE.md` first.
- `frontend/`: the dashboard (Next.js, React). Read `frontend/AGENTS.md` first.
- `ohif/`: our fork of the OHIF DICOM viewer.
Area rules in `.claude/rules/` load by themselves when you open files in that area.

## Run and check
- `poe --help` lists the dev tasks (`poe cloud-up`, `poe cloud-migrate`, `poe backend-integration-tests`, `poe frontend-test`).
- Backend unit tests: `scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh cloud` (or `client`).
- Frontend: `npm run lint`, `npm run check-types`, `npm run test:unit` in `frontend/`.
- Use fake seed data only (factories and TestDataCreator), never real customer data.

## Changes and PRs
- One change per PR. Title: `[FE] RH-1234: what changes for the user` (`[BE]` for backend).
- Cloud, client and sdk CI run on push; frontend CI runs on pull requests.
- Fill in `.github/pull_request_template.md`.

## Knowledge
How does X work, or why is it like this? Use the `kb` skill. It searches the R&D brain (RhinoHealth/rnd-kb) and
cites pages as path@sha. If a page is wrong, propose a fix.

# How a code run reaches the on-prem client

**In short.** The client runs inside the customer's network and opens the connection to the cloud; the cloud never
connects in. Work for the client travels back over that reverse gRPC stream, and the client's handlers run it next to
the customer's data.

## Step by step

## Why it is built this way
Customer networks don't accept inbound connections, and patient data stays on the customer's side.

- The protos in `common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc/` are a contract with clients already installed at customers.

`client/rhinoOnPrem/rhinoAgentRpc/handlers/`, `cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoAgentRpc/`

# ADR-0002: Each agent run gets its own fresh VM

## Context
Agents read untrusted input (tickets, code, web pages) and need Docker for FCP Lab. Anthropic's hosted and
self-hosted agent environments are not available to ZDR organizations.

## Decision
Every run (a Nova ticket, a bug fix, a CI fix) gets a new EC2 VM in the ai-agents AWS account, in one of three
sizes (lite, full, wide), taken from a warm pool and destroyed when the run ends. A VM waiting on a person is
stopped, and after 72 hours destroyed with its work saved.

## Consequences
- Nothing from one run (a process, a file, a cached secret) can reach the next one.
- A run starts in about a minute from the warm pool; stopped VMs cost only their disk.
- Firecracker microVMs are a Q1 test.

code.text:
---
name: kb
description: "Use when you need to know how part of Rhino's system works, why it was built that way, or what was decided. Searches the R&D brain (RhinoHealth/rnd-kb), answers with citations as path@sha, and proposes a fix when a page is wrong."
when_to_use: "Questions like 'how does a code run reach the on-prem client?', 'why does cloud CI run on push?', 'what did we decide about agent VMs?'. Also before planning a change in an area you don't know well."
argument-hint: "[question, or a file path to find pages about it]"
allowed-tools: Bash(kb search *) Bash(kb show *) Read
---
# kb: the R&D brain

The brain is a small set of owned pages about how our system works and why. It holds reasons and decisions the
code doesn't show, so search it even when you feel sure.

1. `kb search "<question>"`; add `--path <file>` when you are about to change that file. Read the top pages with
   `kb show <path>`.
2. Weigh each page by its confidence and reviewed date. `low` or overdue means a lead, not a fact: confirm it in
   the code before you rely on it.
3. Cite each claim as `rnd-kb/<path>@<sha>`, exactly as the search prints it.
4. If the brain has no answer, say so plainly and say where you looked. Don't fill the gap from memory.
5. If a page is wrong or missing something you just confirmed: people run `kb propose <path>` and the page owner
   reviews it; agents add it to the PR's "harness suggestions" section instead.

title: [Shai] Send owners a weekly Slack digest of overdue pages
what: A weekly workflow in rnd-kb runs `kb freshness`, which groups overdue pages by owner and posts one short Slack message per owner. Pages more than 2× overdue read as low confidence everywhere.
why: Pages go stale quietly. A small weekly nudge to the right person keeps them current without a review meeting, and treating very stale pages as low keeps agents from trusting them.
how: Add src/kb_tools/freshness.py (sketch below) behind `kb freshness [--dry-run]`; OWNERS.yml gives each owner's Slack user or channel.
Add .github/workflows/freshness.yml in rnd-kb: cron `17 6 * * 1` (Monday morning, odd minute), main only, secret SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.
Create the Slack app "Rhino Brain" now with only chat:write (ask the Slack workspace admin); the bot tickets later add Socket Mode and read scopes to the same app.
No page edits: search, the index and the bot use effective_confidence from the schema, so a page more than 2× overdue reads as low until its owner reviews it.
First two weeks in --dry-run (prints the messages); check the wording with two owners before posting.

code.text:
# rnd-kb-tooling/src/kb_tools/freshness.py — weekly digest of overdue pages, one message per owner
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date

from slack_sdk import WebClient

from kb_tools.kb import load_owners, load_pages  # pages parsed with schema.Page

PAGE_URL = "https://github.com/RhinoHealth/rnd-kb/blob/main/{path}"


def digest(kb_dir: str, today: date) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    by_owner: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    for path, page in load_pages(kb_dir):
        if page.due() >= today:
            continue
        late = (today - page.due()).days
        note = " (now read as low)" if page.effective_confidence(today) != page.confidence else ""
        by_owner[page.owner].append(f"• <{PAGE_URL.format(path=path)}|{page.title}>: {late} days overdue{note}")
    return by_owner


def post(kb_dir: str, token: str, dry_run: bool) -> None:
    owners = load_owners(kb_dir)  # OWNERS.yml: owner -> Slack user or channel ID
    client = WebClient(token=token)
    for owner, lines in digest(kb_dir, date.today()).items():
        text = "These brain pages are due for a check. Read, fix, then update `reviewed`:\n" + "\n".join(lines)
        if dry_run:
            print(owner, text, sep="\n")
            continue
        client.chat_postMessage(channel=owners[owner].slack, text=text)

title: [Shai] Comment on fcp PRs that touch code a brain page describes
what: A small workflow in fcp matches each pull request's changed files against the applies_to globs in rnd-kb's index.json and posts, or updates, one comment listing the pages and owners to check.
why: Code changes are the main reason pages go stale. A note on the PR, while the author still has the context, is the cheapest moment to fix a page.
how: Add `kb touched --index index.json --files changed.txt` to rnd-kb-tooling: prints a short markdown list (page, owner, which file matched), or nothing.
Add .github/workflows/kb-pages.yml in fcp (sketch below). It is information only: never a required check, and it posts nothing when no page matches.
It uses the rhino-kb app token (contents:read on rnd-kb and rnd-kb-tooling, pull-requests:write on fcp); DevOps adds KB_APP_ID and KB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY to fcp's secrets.
One comment per PR, edited in place on each push, so it never adds noise. Agent PRs get it too; Nova reads it as a hint.

code.text:
# fcp/.github/workflows/kb-pages.yml — tells the author which brain pages describe the code they changed
name: kb-pages
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, ready_for_review]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  pages:
    runs-on: fcp-runner-set
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5 # pin by SHA
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v6
      - id: app
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v2
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.KB_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.KB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          owner: RhinoHealth
          repositories: rnd-kb,rnd-kb-tooling,fcp
      - name: Find pages for the changed files and comment
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app.outputs.token }}
          BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          git diff --name-only "$BASE"...HEAD > changed.txt
          gh api repos/RhinoHealth/rnd-kb/contents/index.json --jq .content | base64 -d > index.json
          uvx --from "git+https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@github.com/RhinoHealth/rnd-kb-tooling" \
            kb touched --index index.json --files changed.txt > comment.md
          if [ -s comment.md ]; then
            gh pr comment "$PR" --body-file comment.md --edit-last --create-if-none
          fi

title: [Shai] Run BRAIN-QA: retrieval on every rnd-kb PR, judged answers nightly
needs: G0: an evals key at the LLM gateway; G1: the eval results store (JSON to S3, pass rates as metrics) and a runner that reaches the gateway
what: A runner in rnd-kb-tooling scores BRAIN-QA: retrieval (a source page in kb search's top 5) on every rnd-kb PR, and judged answers nightly. It also proves no golden-set question was indexed.
why: The targets are the right page in the top 5 for at least 85% of questions and a correct answer for at least 80%. Running retrieval on every KB change catches an edit that hides an answer.
how: Add evals/brain_qa.py (sketch below) with `--mode retrieval` (no model calls; a step in kb-lint's CI that reads the golden set with the rhino-kb app and prints only case ids and totals) and `--mode answers` (nightly).

Answers come from `claude -p` with the kb plugin (Sonnet 5.5, low effort) until the bot ships; then the runner calls the bot's answer() (G6-21). The judge is Sonnet 5.5 at medium with PASS/FAIL per answer point, checked first against Shai's own labels on 10 answers.
Leak check: fail if any question's 8-word runs appear in an rnd-kb page, or if the golden-set repo is in any search or bot source list.
Write results JSON to the G1 eval store and the two numbers to the check summary; retrieval below 85% fails the PR.
The nightly job runs on the agents' runner set through the LLM gateway (evals key); the runner holds no Anthropic key.

code.text:
# rnd-kb-tooling/evals/brain_qa.py — sketch; prints ids and totals only, never question text (CI logs are visible)
import json
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from kb_tools.search import search  # the same ranking `kb search` uses
from kb_tools.text import normalise, word_runs  # small helpers, omitted here


def retrieval(cases: list[dict], kb_dir: str) -> float:
    answerable = [c for c in cases if c["expect"] == "answer"]
    hits = 0
    for case in answerable:
        top5 = [hit.path for hit in search(kb_dir, case["question"], limit=5)]
        hits += any(page in top5 for page in case["source_pages"])
    return hits / len(answerable)


def leaked(cases: list[dict], kb_dir: str) -> list[str]:
    pages = " ".join(normalise(p.read_text()) for p in Path(kb_dir).rglob("*.md"))
    return [c["id"] for c in cases if any(run in pages for run in word_runs(c["question"], 8))]


def ask(question: str) -> str:
    # until the bot ships; then: from bot.app import answer
    out = subprocess.run(
        ["claude", "-p", question, "--plugin-dir", "plugin", "--model", "claude-sonnet-5-5",
         "--effort", "low", "--output-format", "json"],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
    )
    return json.loads(out.stdout)["result"]

title: [Platform] Brain bot v0: Bolt in Socket Mode + Agent SDK, read-only, cited
needs: G0: LLM gateway with the brain-bot key; G3: the same pattern as Nova's Slack app (Socket Mode, no public endpoint), not its code: that app is TypeScript (Bolt 5), this bot is Bolt for Python
what: A small Python service in rnd-kb-tooling/bot/ answers @Rhino Brain mentions in allow-listed public channels, using the Agent SDK with read-only tools over mirrors of rnd-kb and fcp, and replies in the thread with citations or says it doesn't know. It stays Python, unlike the agent platform, because it imports kb_tools in-process, so it ranks pages and redacts exactly like the kb CLI and BRAIN-QA.
why: Most questions are asked in Slack, not in Claude Code. Claude Tag isn't available under ZDR, so the bot is our own app, with the same brain and the same citation rule.
how: bot/app.py (sketch below): Bolt for Python in Socket Mode (no public endpoint); Agent SDK with tools limited to Read, Grep and Glob (add an in-process kb_search tool over kb_tools.search, the CLI's ranking), no setting sources, structured output {answer, citations, unverified}. Our code posts the reply; the model never calls Slack.
Sonnet 5.5 at low effort, with a prompt line to search even when confident. ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is the LLM gateway, which adds the brain-bot key.

Walls in code: answer only in BRAIN_CHANNELS (public engineering channels from G6-01); refuse questions that match the PHI patterns or deny-list (reuse kb scan); redact deny-list terms in replies; never read private channels.
Every citation must resolve to a file in the mirror at its sha; the code drops any that don't, and with none left it replies "I don't know" and where to ask.
Point BRAIN-QA's answer mode at answer() and run it once (targets 85% retrieval, 80% correct).

code.text:
# rnd-kb-tooling/bot/app.py — sketch. Runs on inf-rhinohealth; ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is the LLM gateway (it adds the key).
import asyncio
import os

from claude_agent_sdk import ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage, query
from slack_bolt.adapter.socket_mode.async_handler import AsyncSocketModeHandler
from slack_bolt.async_app import AsyncApp

from bot.citations import ANSWER, format_reply, keep_resolvable  # ANSWER: {answer, citations, unverified} schema
from kb_tools.scan import has_blocked_terms, redact  # same PHI patterns and deny-list as kb-lint

app = AsyncApp(token=os.environ["SLACK_BOT_TOKEN"])
CHANNELS = set(os.environ["BRAIN_CHANNELS"].split(","))  # public engineering channels only (DATA-SCOPE.md)
OPTIONS = ClaudeAgentOptions(
    model="claude-sonnet-5-5", effort="low",
    cwd="/mirror/rnd-kb", add_dirs=["/mirror/fcp"],  # read-only git mirrors, refreshed every 10 minutes
    tools=["Read", "Grep", "Glob"], setting_sources=[],  # no Bash, no writes, no web, no local config
    system_prompt=open("/app/prompts/brain.md").read(),
    output_format={"type": "json_schema", "schema": ANSWER})


async def answer(question: str) -> dict:
    async for message in query(prompt=question, options=OPTIONS):
        if isinstance(message, ResultMessage):
            return keep_resolvable(message.structured_output)  # drops citations missing at the mirror's sha


@app.event("app_mention")
async def on_mention(event, say):
    if event["channel"] not in CHANNELS or has_blocked_terms(event["text"]):
        return await say(thread_ts=event["ts"], text="I can't answer that here. Ask in a public engineering channel, without patient or customer details.")
    await say(thread_ts=event["ts"], text=redact(format_reply(await answer(event["text"]))))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(AsyncSocketModeHandler(app, os.environ["SLACK_APP_TOKEN"]).start_async())
